lines.text: Many web frameworks trust a header that proxies never clean.
A proxy sits in front of your app and adds headers telling it who the real visitor is.
lines.title: Normal flow

lines.text: Most proxies clean X-Forwarded headers but pass the newer Forwarded header through untouched.
lines.title: What proxies do

lines.text: Rails, Spring and Jetty can read Forwarded by default, and may trust it over the proxy's own header.
lines.title: Frameworks affected

lines.text: Attackers can fake their IP, bypass limits, send password-reset links to the wrong site, or poison caches.
lines.title: What can go wrong

lines.text: Spring Boot four point two now reads only X-Forwarded headers by default.
lines.title: A fix lands

lines.text: Make every layer agree on which headers to trust, and drop the rest at the first proxy.
lines.title: Takeaways
